page: Amazon Web Services u7i-6tb.112xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8477C processors operating at a base frequency of 1.9 GHz. It features 224 physical cores yielding 448 vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled, accompanied by 105 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and instruction extensions including AVX-512 and AMX. The instance supplies 6,144 GB (6 TB) of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5 memory, which equates to 13.71 GB of RAM per vCPU. No local storage is included with the instance, requiring all persistent storage to be attached remotely over the network, which maintains a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. It contains no GPUs.

Benchmark data reflects exceptional performance in heavily parallelized and memory-dense operations. Multi-core compute performance sits in the top tier, exemplified by a stress-ng multi-core score of 358,896.17 and PassMark CPU score of 158,955.78, alongside top-tier results in extended instruction and encryption evaluations. In-memory throughput is notable, with Redis SET operations achieving 375.58 million operations per second and cached read memory bandwidth reaching 29,269.53 GB/sec, complemented by large-block read bandwidth of 840.11 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core processing metrics, such as a stress-ng single-core score of 1,978.5 and Geekbench single-core score of 2,021.0, fall within standard ranges due to the moderate 1.9 GHz clock rate.

Given its massive memory footprint and high parallel compute density, the instance provides significant resource consolidation for enterprise scale applications. However, the absence of local disks necessitates reliance on networked volumes for all I/O requirements, and generative LLM token generation remains bounded by CPU execution speeds. AWS u7i-6tb.112xlarge is primarily suited for large in-memory databases like SAP HANA, extensive real-time analytical caches, and large enterprise memory-bound transactional workloads.
